review_items.rationale:
Reviewed fixed artifact dddede686d1a4bdb87cd514ac7e8f137 version 1, its accepted claim/bindings version 1, fixed plan and complete harness, and retained execution 5ef2409f00cd47c983439ae485dde415. The measured event implication is violated; Go tests_passed only means the observation harness completed.

Responsibility: s_joint_contract and s_conf_contract assign implicit exit to Raft, contrasting explicit exit assigned to the application. s_auto_ownership requires automatic transition when possible. Generic proposal retry language does not make an unrelated ordinary proposal a prerequisite of that owned transition. The observation is not an invented ten-tick deadline: the witness is a recurrent legal execution after transfer expiration.

Entry and history: all three RawNodes start from the same declared index-1/term-1 agreed snapshot and HardState, with no crash. A real Campaign elects node 1 at term 2 and commits/applies its empty entry at index 2. Actual ProposeConfChange creates the implicit removal at index 3. The application starts transfer to node 2 only after observing this committed entry and checking node 2 Match equals the leader tail. The call is serialized between Ready and Advance, with entries already persisted. This permits the relevant overlap rather than draining it away. The leader then applies the committed change and Advance completes application; the active transfer causes the generated exit proposal to be rejected by the ordinary proposal handler. Exactly one actually emitted MsgTimeoutNow is lost, with all later messages delivered through the same queue. No fabricated network support or private protocol writes occur. Synchronous MemoryStorage represents completed storage in this no-crash scope. All Ready work is persisted before delivery and applied before Advance; RawNode has no independent goroutine or shutdown work. This meets the stricter Ready contract as well as the general usage instructions.

Correlation and admission: overlap=true selects the principal scenario independently of results. case_id plus config_index identifies the same operation in admitted, cycle_start and cycle_result; there is one of each in this history. Admission actually records implicit=true, applied=3, auto_leave=true, transfer=2, one loss and drained work. cycle_start follows the admitted applied value by reference and records transfer=0, leader=true and drained work. Actual configuration events show incoming voters [1,2] and outgoing [1,2,3] on all participants. The result records cycle_closed=true and auto_leave=true, so the independently monitored implication fails. The control is excluded by its predeclared overlap=false, not by whether it succeeded.

Observation and recurrence: I reassembled the retained Go JSON Output chunks and independently parsed both before/after strings; they are equal in the principal scenario. These are fresh immutable snapshots read from the live RawNodes, not cached exports. The recursive traversal includes RawNode previous states and stepsOnAdvance, raft term/vote/role/timers/read queues, log indexes and unstable state, full MemoryStorage hard state/snapshot/entries, membership, progress, inflight buffer and accounting, and caller loss policy and queue. All nodes are term 2 with applied=applying=commit=last=3, no unstable entries or pending snapshots, no Ready/messages/Advance callbacks, and empty transport. Leader progress for all voters is Match=3, Next=4, StateReplicate, RecentActive=true, with zero inflight count/bytes. Automatic-exit size accounting is uncommittedSize=0; pendingConfIndex=3 and applied=3 satisfy its configuration eligibility. Transfer is zero. The only excluded fields are logger/traceLogger, MemoryStorage read callStats and its unlocked mutex. Source shows these counters are increment-only diagnostics, logging is an output sink, default tracing is inactive, and all storage calls here are serialized. Slice capacities and pointer allocation identities do not select the heartbeat-only behavior; the same raft receivers, role callbacks and storage objects remain installed.

The suffix is ten repetitions of Tick for nodes 1,2,3 followed by complete processing of every Ready and network message. Every round is observed drained and carries only MsgHeartbeat/MsgHeartbeatResp; none is dropped. At each boundary follower electionElapsed is zero because heartbeats reset it. Leader heartbeatElapsed is zero and electionElapsed returns to zero after its configured quorum-check period. Heartbeat replies keep all voters active, so CheckQuorum does not change role. Both quorum sets are available. The captured randomized election timeouts are unchanged and no election threshold is reached; global randomness is only consumed by resetRandomizedElectionTimeout, unreachable on these same-term heartbeat paths. No callbacks, timers, transport work or application work are withheld. Internal MsgBeat and MsgCheckQuorum are generated by Tick, processed synchronously and accounted for by source tracing. The finite harness loop's stop counter merely chooses observation boundaries; it does not influence the target or message policy. Its diagnostic counters and observation flags likewise do not schedule target work. Thus the same external tick schedule can repeat with the same relevant state and effects. With last index fixed and no pending log/application work, no hidden exit proposal is waiting to commit. This closes the continuation premise for the selected history rather than deriving nontermination from finite waiting alone.

Cause and counterevidence: appliedTo proposes empty exit but Step rejects while leadTransferee is nonzero; abortLeaderTransfer clears only that blocker. Empty Ready/Advance does not manufacture MsgStorageApplyResp, and heartbeat processing supplies no configuration retry. The no-transfer control applies exit at index 4. After the principal observation a normal proposal commits at index 4 and its application triggers exit at index 5. Successful new leadership could likewise provide another entry. These mechanisms explain recovery under extra events and limit the consequence; they do not supply an owed event within the established idle reliable suffix. No correspondence issue was found for this scoped witness; this is a provisional semantic assessment, not an independent correctness proof.
review_items.report_title: 领导权转移失败后，隐式联合配置可能失去自动退出触发
review_items.report_answer: 在已应用的隐式联合配置与领导权转移重叠、仅丢失一次 TimeoutNow 的历史中，转移超时后出现完整状态重复的心跳执行周期，AutoLeave 仍为 true。后续普通提案可以触发退出；本结果限定为自动继续执行责任，不声称共识安全破坏。
limitations: One synchronous no-crash configuration and schedule are checked; async storage, restart and arbitrary membership histories are not established.
The infinite-extension inference applies to the audited deterministic heartbeat suffix and its actual state projection; it is not a general temporal model checker.
Global availability consequences and operational prevalence are not measured.
The no-transfer control exits automatically; the failed-transfer case exits when a later ordinary proposal supplies a new application completion.
The implementation can therefore still commit ordinary work. This is not a demonstrated consensus safety failure or total cluster outage.
